unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the experimental steel at -196 °C is estimated to be 32 mJ/m², which still totally suppresses DIMT but enables the occurrence of mechanical twinning; mechanical twinning is reported as the main deformation mechanism for high-Mn steels when SFE is between 18 and 35 mJ/m².
Two-stage work-hardening exponents at -196 °C from the Hollomon analysis: n1 = 0.204 (low-strain region) and n2 = 0.448 (high-strain region), the largest of the three tensile temperatures.
Reported linear temperature dependence of tensile strength (T in °C): UTS = 813.0 - 2.36×T and YS = 474.6 - 2.05×T (Fig. 2c); both YS and UTS increase linearly as deformation temperature decreases.
At -196 °C the tensile necking point (where true stress equals the work hardening rate, σtrue = dσtrue/dεtrue) occurs at the highest stress and true strain among the three temperatures.

The region flanking the primary crack is transgranular: misorientation analysis across the crack (Fig. 10c) shows a misorientation difference of less than 15° between the regions on both sides of the crack, i.e., they belonged to the same grain before cracking.
